items.note: PLS-SEM survey of 1,443 Egyptian tourism students linking perceived ChatGPT risks to creative thinking, plus an SPSS quasi-experiment comparing ChatGPT users; creative thinking is probably a self-report scale and the quasi-experiment's arms and size are not described, so it may be out (self_report_only) at full text.

Children who trained with Co-Art (AI turns a spoken sentence into an abstract image that inspires a second drawing) drew images rated richer and more imaginative than a non-trained group; assignment and N not stated, sample likely small.

Online social-network experiment in which human-only, AI-only, and hybrid 5x5 networks iteratively modify stories, with human-rated creativity and collective diversity; human exposure to AI is by network composition, so the full text must show whether participants were assigned to hybrid vs human-only networks (other versions report 879 to 1,473 humans; same study as arXiv 2502.17962 and CogSci 2025).

43 expert NLP researchers were randomly assigned to execute an LLM-generated or expert-written research idea, and blind reviewers scored the executed projects on novelty, excitement, effectiveness, and overall; N below 50, and follow-up to Si et al.'s ideation study.

Single-group pretest-posttest in a Chilean school: students aged 12-13 wrote songs with ChatGPT and took the TTCT before and after (flexibility and originality rose, fluency fell slightly); no control group and no N in the abstract, so likely fails eligibility.

120 undergraduates in a character design course were assigned to GAI with structured design-thinking strategy, GAI without strategy, or traditional learning; design achievement (possibly a rated design score) plus self-efficacy and problem solving, so check whether design achievement rates creativity of the designs.

46 participants completed creative design tasks in a serious game with or without generative AI; creative outputs were scored for quantity, quality, elaboration, and integrity alongside physiological stress measures; N below 50 and assignment not stated.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC); search notes describe 128 participants in a generative-AI design group vs a traditional design group on brainstorming and TRIZ tasks, with creativity output scores plus fNIRS and facial expressions; assignment unconfirmed.

132 nursing undergraduates randomly divided into GenAI interactive-teaching and control groups (66 each); outcomes are higher-order thinking skills and AI literacy, likely self-report scales with no creative task, so probably out (self_report_only or no_creativity_or_diversity_outcome) at full text.

Controlled experiment (N = 398) with Human-Only, Standard Chatbot, Engage-to-Unlock, and Time-Matched Unlock conditions on a writing task followed by passage evaluation; outcomes are time allocation, prompting, and evaluation accuracy, with no creativity, quality, or diversity score of the writing reported.
